properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (measured on flo2.io and main): reasoning_report's whole-design summary came back with names as "…" because the budget's 0 rung blanks every string longer than 80 characters (NEVER_TRIM_BELOW guards ids, not names), and the claims page takes the budget first, leaving the summary 0 room; argument names (with pinpoint cites) are routinely over 80
properties.source: Public legal-case trial friction file F11; reasoning_report on flo2 design dbf39096640c196e (budget_chars 3000), 2026-10-26; reflow2 main reply_budget.rs
properties.statement:
OBSERVED (public legal-case trial, F11): the whole-design reasoning_report cut 78 text fields to 0 characters ("WITHHELD TO FIT"), and names in still_contested came back as "…". It was readable only claim by claim.

MEASURED on design dbf39096640c196e (reasoning_report, budget_chars 3000; the trial saw the same 78 at flo2's default): the budget block reads full_chars 30005, fields_trimmed 78, prose_limit 0, summary_room 0, with "the 0 characters the claims leave". Every name that SURVIVED is at most 80 characters (80, 79, 71, 69 measured). Every name over 80 reads "…".

Code at main, reply_budget.rs: truncate_prose (about line 119) keeps a string whole when it has at most NEVER_TRIM_BELOW = 80 characters (line 103). Otherwise it keeps `limit` characters, which is 0 at the last rung, and appends "…". The floor's own comment says it was sized against ids and hashes ("reflow2's longest id is well under this, and a sha256: hash is 71"), and the artifact claims "names, ids and enum values survive every rung".

CANDIDATES:
(1) The 0 rung blanks long names. Confirmed by the 80-character boundary in the data.
(2) The claims page is filled first and the summary gets what is left. Confirmed (summary_room 0). It is why the 0 rung is reached at all.
(3) flo2's budget is too small. Contributing only: the whole answer is about 10% over flo2's default.
(4) The design has too much evidence. It adds rows but is not the cause: ids at full precision fit, only names were dropped.

CLASS: a floor tuned for identifiers is applied to names, and in an argument a name is the statement a reader recognises. Options:
- the last rung cuts to the floor (80 characters plus "…") rather than to 0;
- or `name` keys are exempt like ids;
- and the summary is given reserved room before the claims page is filled.
Not built; awaits the owner.
